newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, looks to consolidate.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, looks to consolidate.

text.p: There was little encouragement for a follow-through to New York's late Friday rally on Monday with Europe and, later, Comex no more than steady, dealers said.
"After all the moves last week, it would not be surprising if they took a breather this week," one dealer said.
Platinum, having given the upward impetus to the complex, continued to weaken from a $407-bid high on Friday despite a strike notice by workers at Russia's Norilsk mining and refining complex.
Bullion fixed at $362.15 per ounce up from $361.80 in the morning and $358.60 on Friday when the correction from recent highs was in full swing.
"Gold has held steady while platinum and palladium have come off. Technically its top looks to be around $365," a dealer said.
However he added that gold may have seen the high in its current phase and if it corrected, a return to $358.00 was technically feasible.
The Comex April contract was down $0.90 at $364.20 in modest volume at the 1500 GMT fixing.
Platinum was indicated down $2.00 at $387.00/$388.00 having opened a dollar above the Friday close but showing none of the bounce seen late last week.
The correction in platinum on Friday was much more dramatic than in the other metals and reflected the precariousness of its rise from around $371.00 last Monday to Friday's high.
"The push (to $407) in Tokyo on Friday might be the last blow-out of that phase. It could take a breather now," a dealer said.
Technical analysts warned that since platinum challenged its highs from May last year on Friday, a period of much more volatile prices was likely.
There was little price impact from a decision to strike in 10 days time by workers at Russia's nickel-platinum-palladium mining and refining combine Norilsk at the weekend over unpaid wages.
"It was pretty much in the price already," a dealer said.
But there were no reported moves to bring Russian and Japanese negotiators to the table to begin talks on platinum and palladium export contracts for 1997.
Palladium also lost ground to be indicated at $149.60/$150.60, down $1.40 and silver was up nine cents with gold at $5.32/$5.34.
